title: The shuffle that plays favourites
hook: Swap every card with a random spot. It feels fair. Count the runs.

knows: 3 cards can be in 6 orders (shown on the stage)
doesNotKnow: that a plausible shuffle can be unfair

misconception: Swapping each card with a random position gives a fair shuffle.
objective: The learner can explain that swapping each position with any of 3 positions has 27 equally likely runs, which cannot split evenly over 6 orders (4s and 5s), while swapping only with an unplaced card has 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 runs, one per order.

claims.text: Swapping each of 3 positions with any of the 3 positions gives 27 equally likely runs: ACB, BAC and BCA come up 5 times each, ABC, CAB and CBA 4 times each.
claims.source: Exhaustive enumeration, no randomness: the stage and the builder's node script (scratchpad checks/all.mjs) list all 3 x 3 x 3 runs; counts ABC 4, ACB 5, BAC 5, BCA 5, CAB 4, CBA 4.

claims.text: Those three orders are 25% more likely than the others.
27 runs cannot split evenly over 6 orders, because 27 is not a multiple of 6.
claims.source: 27 / 6 = 4.5. Equal probability for 6 orders from 27 equally likely runs would need each order to get 4.5 runs.

claims.text: Swapping only with a card not yet placed has 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 runs, exactly one per order: this is the Fisher-Yates shuffle.
claims.source: Exhaustive enumeration on the stage (6 runs, each order once). Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 2, 3.4.2, Algorithm P; CLRS 3rd ed. 5.3, RANDOMIZE-IN-PLACE: each permutation has probability 1/n!.

claims.text: A fair shuffle needs a number of equally likely runs that the number of orders divides evenly.
claims.source: If R equally likely runs map to n! orders with equal probability, each order gets R/n! runs, which must be a whole number. (Necessary, not sufficient.)

recall.question: A shuffle of 4 cards makes 4 x 4 x 4 x 4 = 256 equally likely runs. There are 24 orders. Can every order be equally likely?
options: Yes, with that many runs it evens out
No: 256 is not a multiple of 24
Only if the cards start sorted
recall.why: Each order would need 256 / 24 runs, which is not a whole number, so some orders must come up more often.
